title: Long-term effects of maternal deprivation on cholinergic system in rat brain.
ehr_evidence: The study used Wistar rats and brain tissue for biochemical and immunohistochemical analysis.
summary: Experimental study examining the long-term effects of maternal separation on acetylcholinesterase activity and cholinergic fiber density in the brains of Wistar rats.
key_findings: AChE activity significantly decreased in the cortex (P<0.05) and significantly increased in the hippocampus (P<0.05) compared to controls.
No significant change in AChE activity was observed in the thalamus or caudate nuclei.
ChAT positive fiber density significantly increased in the hippocampal CA1 region, with no change in CA3 or dentate gyrus.
ChAT positive fiber density significantly decreased in the retrosplenial cortex.
population: male Wistar rats, postnatal day 9 to 60
limitations: single 24-hour maternal separation protocol on postnatal day 9
limited to specific brain regions and cholinergic markers
